turns: Which hubs in the Midwest are most exposed to winter disruption?
results.answer: Minneapolis (MSP) is the most exposed Midwest hub to winter disruption. Its winter score is 48.2, which is moderate, not high. Chicago (CHI) is next at 39.9, then Detroit (DTW) at 37.4 and Kansas City (MCI) at 33.8, all moderate. Indianapolis (30.7) and Columbus (30.1) are low. MSP is driven by 146.4 freeze days/yr (min temp <= 0 C) and 20.4 days/yr with snowfall >= 1 cm. CHI has 103.6 freeze days and 18.6 snow days/yr. Chicago and Detroit are separated by 2.5 points, so their order is not meaningful. The same goes for Indianapolis and Columbus.

turns: Compare Miami and Houston in terms of hurricane and flood exposure.
results.answer: Miami has the higher hurricane/wind exposure and Houston has much higher flood exposure. Wind: Miami scores 51.9 (moderate) and Houston 43.1 (moderate). Miami's score is driven mainly by 11 FEMA wind declarations over 20 years, against 8 for Houston. Flood: Houston scores 74.7 (high) and Miami 32.4 (low). Houston has 23.6 days/yr with at least 25 mm of rain, against 9.2 for Miami. It also has 4.2 days/yr with at least 50 mm, against 2.2, and 7 FEMA flood declarations, against 2. Houston's composite score is 39.0 and Miami's is 22.7. Both are moderate or low in absolute terms, even though Houston's flood score is high.

turns: What percentage of days in Denver last year had snowfall?
results.answer: In 2025, Denver had measurable snowfall (at least 0.1 cm) on 37 of 365 days, which is 10.1% of days. Snowfall of at least 1 cm occurred on 17 days, or 4.7%.

turns: Why is the Dallas hub's weather disruption risk high?
results.answer: Dallas's composite Weather Disruption Risk Score is 36.5, which is moderate, not high. The moderate band starts at 33. It ranks 2nd of 14 hubs, so it is high relative to the network but not in absolute terms. Flood and heavy rain contribute most, at 16.3 points. The flood score is 54.3, driven by 16.2 days/yr with at least 25 mm of rain and 3.6 days/yr with at least 50 mm. Heat adds 6.8 points, from 54.6 days/yr above 35 C. Wind adds 9.9 points, with 5 FEMA wind-type declarations over 20 years and 18.2 days/yr with gusts of 60 km/h or more. Winter adds only 3.5 points, and its score of 11.7 is low.

turns: Rank the Midwest hubs by flood exposure.
results.answer: Chicago's flood score is 30.8, which is low and just under the moderate cutoff of 33. It ranked second among Midwest hubs in the earlier ranking, and that order against Minneapolis was a close call. The biggest driver is 7 FEMA flood/severe-storm declarations over 2006-2025, worth 18.7 of the 30.8 points. Rain adds less: 5.8 days/yr with at least 25 mm (10.1 points) and 0.4 days/yr with at least 50 mm (2.0 points). Chicago's composite score is 25.9, also low, and ranks 7 of 14 in the network.

turns: Which three hubs have the highest overall weather disruption risk?
results.answer: The top three hubs by composite Weather Disruption Risk Score are Houston (HOU) at 39.0, Dallas (DFW) at 36.5 and Newark (EWR) at 33.4. All three are only "moderate" in absolute terms (low is below 33, high is 66 or above). They rank at the top relative to the rest of the network, but none is high-risk. Houston's main drivers are 23.6 days/yr with at least 25 mm of rain and 8 FEMA wind declarations over 20 years. Dallas's are 16.2 heavy-rain days/yr and 54.6 days/yr above 35 C. Newark's are 7 FEMA wind declarations and 12.2 heavy-rain days/yr. Houston and Dallas are 2.5 points apart, so their order isn't meaningful. Dallas and Newark are 3.1 points apart, which is just over the 3-point close-call threshold, so that order is less certain than a clear gap.

turns: Which hubs face the biggest hurricane risk?
results.answer: Miami has the highest hurricane/wind score in the network at 51.9, which is moderate. Newark is next at 43.3 and Houston at 43.1, both moderate. Dallas is moderate at 39.6, and Atlanta is low at 26.6. No hub reaches the high level (66 or above), so Miami is highest relative to the others, not high in absolute terms. Miami's score is driven mainly by 11 FEMA hurricane, tropical storm, tornado and wind declarations in 20 years and 11.8 days/yr with gusts of 60 km/h or more. Newark and Houston are a close call, so their order is not meaningful. Newark's score comes more from gusty days (20.4 days/yr at 60 km/h or more) than from declarations (7). Houston has 8 declarations and 10.8 gusty days/yr.

turns: Where is extreme heat the biggest problem for us?
results.answer: Phoenix (PHX) is the clear heat problem. It scores 100 out of 100 (high) with 137.4 days/yr at or above 35 C. Dallas (DFW) is a distant second at 45.5 (moderate) with 54.6 days/yr above 35 C. Houston (HOU, 22.3, 26.8 days/yr) and Denver (DEN, 14.8, 17.8 days/yr) are both low. Heat resilience investment should go to Phoenix first, then Dallas.

turns: Compare Denver, Minneapolis and Chicago for winter risk.
results.answer: Denver has the highest winter score of the three at 53.9, then Minneapolis at 48.2 and Chicago at 39.9. All three are 'moderate', not 'high'. Denver leads because it has 152.2 freeze days/yr, 22.4 days/yr with snowfall of 1 cm or more, and 1 FEMA winter declaration. Minneapolis has 146.4 freeze days/yr and 20.4 snow days/yr, with no FEMA winter declarations. Chicago has 103.6 freeze days/yr and 18.6 snow days/yr. Chicago is close to Detroit (37.4) in the network ranking, so the order of those two is not meaningful. On the composite score, which covers all hazards, all three hubs are 'low' (Denver 27.1, Chicago 25.9, Minneapolis 25.8).

turns: How many days in 2024 did Phoenix reach 35 C or more, as a share of the year?
results.answer: Phoenix reached 35 C or more on 151 of 366 days in 2024, which is 41.3% of the year. 2024 was a leap year, so the denominator is 366 days. The data had no missing days.

It has 0.0 days/yr with snowfall of 1 cm or more, 0.0 days/yr with 10 cm or more, 1.6 freeze days/yr, and 0 FEMA winter declarations in 20 years. Phoenix's real exposure is heat. Its heat score is 100 (high), with 137.4 days/yr above 35 C. Its composite score is 19.0 (low), which ranks 14th of 14. The hubs with the most winter exposure are Denver (53.9), Minneapolis (48.2) and Chicago (39.9), all moderate.
